# Phase One — Unbounded Brainstorm

The Awtsmoos renews every frame and every test; this plan seeks every vessel where motion, story, persistence, and pixels may still conceal unfinished work.

## Possible completion fronts

- Repository archaeology: source graph, imports, scripts, generated proofs, ignored media, worktree state, stale checkpoints, and hidden regressions.
- Character identity: neutral facial landmarks, head shape, body mass, posture, hair, wardrobe, reusable saved identity, and separation from performance state.
- Face performance: deterministic blink, gaze, convergence, eye targets, head turn, eyebrow regions, eyelids, phoneme timing, visemes, and mouth geometry.
- Body performance: breathing, lean, weight shift, locomotion, gesture preparation/stroke/hold/follow-through/retraction, and contact locks.
- Geometry readability: hands, fingers, crossed arms, pocket hands, palms, point, wave, shoes, heel/toe/sole direction, garments, hair, sleeve drag, hem lift, and secondary motion.
- Cinematic systems: multiple views, shot vocabulary, automatic framing, camera continuity, title cards, text boxes, captions, dialogue timing, and scene timing.
- Persistence: customizer data, save/load, import/export, startup restoration, transient exclusion, project packaging, and media durability.
- Rendering: preview/export parity, production canvas, browser state, exact dimensions, nonblank PNGs, hashes, frame sampling, and final video/audio metadata.
- Quality: small-scale legibility, visual courts, accessibility, performance, blank-shell detection, cropping, text safety, and narrative clarity.
- Orchestration: sequential agent spawning, isolated scopes, evidence contracts, merge queue, conflict control, reassignment, and master verification.
- Future possibilities: deterministic replay, golden-frame comparisons, automated perceptual metrics, export manifest signing, and richer demo variations.

## Work graph principle

Every feature must trace through source state → normalization → composition → render bridge → geometry → production pixels → persistence → preview → export → test → proof.

No module name, prior report, or passing smoke alone closes a node.
